title: Floating bar: margin, radius, a switch and Hyprland-derived defaults
head: ced627546026
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Cloned notification services cannot see floating-bar margins through the scoped bar facade
leads.consequence: A user cloning/enabling the built-in notifications service gets shell.bar as PluginBarStateApi, which has barSize and position but no barMargins. liveBarMargin stays zero. On a 26px top bar with default floating edge margin 5 and gapsOut 5, a cloned toast begins at 31px, touching the bar's bottom at 31px instead of keeping 5px clearance; with [bar] margin=10, it begins at 31px while the bar ends at 36px, a 5px overlap. The trusted original service gets the real shell.bar and is not affected. Expose a reactive barMargins snapshot on PluginBarStateApi, bind it in pluginBarStateFor, and cover the scoped clone path.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N2; published as finding

leads.summary: Workspace-specific gaps_out values are ignored by the floating bar
leads.consequence: If a Hyprland workspace rule changes gaps_out from the global value, the bar still computes its edge and end margins from hyprctl getoption general:gaps_out; windows on that workspace use the rule instead, so the documented end alignment and matching gaps do not hold. Repro: global gaps_out=10 and workspace rule gaps_out=30, with bar.floating=true and no theme margin gives bar margins top=5, ends=10, while that workspace's tiled windows have 30px gaps. Omarchy's shipped special:scratchpad rule supplies a real workspace override (top=0, other edges variable); it is not a normal tiled workspace, so the repro with an ordinary override is the clearest user-visible condition. Either qualify docs as global-gap defaults or read effective per-workspace gaps where feasible.
leads.triage: not published: workspace-rule gaps_out divergence is niche and pre-existing design since initial head

leads.summary: A valid negative top gaps_out silently freezes all four floating margins at previous values
leads.consequence: Hyprland accepts negative CSS gap edges. If it reports css='-2 12 12 12', the first parsed value n=-2 fails the nonnegative gate; none of gapsOutEdges is updated, even though right/bottom/left are positive. The bar continues using its previous global default (initially 10 on each side) while window layout uses the new gaps. This especially affects a valid configuration with negative top gap and positive side gaps; no error is shown. Handle the four edges independently or document unsupported negative gaps, and test a valid negative-first response.
leads.triage: not published: confirmed Style.qml applyGapsOutJson skips all edges when first value negative; unchanged since earlier reviewed head; negative gaps_out unusual

leads.summary: Two additional shipped guides still promise stable windows beyond the documented gap limit
leads.consequence: At gaps_out=52 with stock 26px horizontal bar, the anchored default margin rounds to 26, exclusiveZone clamps to 1, and the reserved extent is 27px instead of flush 26px; toggling floating therefore moves tiled windows by 1px. docs/omarchy-shell.md:404 now states the limit but the shipped skill and plugin README both unconditionally say windows do not move. Copy the limit/qualification to those two files, not just the shell manual.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F4/N3 nit; published in Documentation

leads.summary: Related PR #13137 collides with the narrowed [bar] parser and its value test
leads.location: shell/Commons/Style.qml:437-447; related open PR #13137 shell/Commons/Style.qml applyShellValues
leads.consequence: #13137 changes applyShellValues to pass every numeric [bar] key through to barOverrides and tests icon-slot/icon-canvas/icon-font/status-slot. This PR instead restricts the branch to size-horizontal/size-vertical/radius plus raw margin, leaving those four keys silently ignored. The same else-if hunk changes in both PRs; if merged by retaining this PR's branch, #13137's added test will fail and its feature is lost; if merging by retaining #13137's generic parseInt, margin lists would be reduced to one integer unless the raw margin branch is preserved. Combine both changes explicitly (margin raw, all other numeric keys parsed) and run both tests. Stacked PR #13140 already shows such a combination in its file patch, so this is a coordination hazard, not a claim that the final integration inevitably regresses.
leads.triage: not published: conditional overlap with #13137 in the same author's stacked series; #13140 already combines

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Follow-up on the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13138#issuecomment-5824376092) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13138#issuecomment-5829005179), checked at head `ced6275`. All five earlier points are resolved; for the large-`gaps_out` point, the qualifier is in the main docs only. No regressions were found in the changed or shared code. One new low-impact finding (the plugin bar facade has no margin), an optional test improvement and some documentation notes follow.

| Earlier point | Status at `ced6275` |
|---|---|
| Popouts and toasts ignore the bar margin | Resolved |
| Docs cite a missing `omarchy bar floating` command | Resolved |
| `"4 8"` example comment wrong for side bars | Resolved |
| Large `gaps_out` limit missing from the docs | Resolved in `docs/omarchy-shell.md` (see Documentation) |
| Optional test improvement: source-text checks | Resolved for the five named breakages, as reproduced here |

**Verified:**
- Popout placement, click forwarding and toast clearance were evaluated from the real `KeyboardPanel.qml` and `notifications/Service.qml` expressions, covering all four bar positions, floating in the gap (uniform and per-side `gaps_out`), theme margins `10` and `"4 8"`, and icon-anchored and `centerOnBar` panels. In all 32 floating cases, the card sits exactly `gap` (5 px) off the bar's outer face and centres on its icon, or on the bar for the clock and weather panels. A click at the icon is forwarded to it with no offset, and toasts keep a 5 px gap from top and right bars. The same evaluation on the base code reproduces the earlier table.
- With a flush bar, and with `floating: false` over a theme margin, popouts, click forwarding and toasts are identical to the base in all 16 cases.
- Moving the window margins and exclusive zone into `BarModel` preserves behaviour: the logic is identical per edge.
- The docs now name the `"floating": true` key under `bar`. `omarchy bar position`, `transparent` and `use` keep that key when they rewrite `shell.json`. The `"4 8"` comment matches `parseWidthSpec` for every position.
- Evaluated with the real `BarModel`: `gaps_out` 50 reserves 26 px, 51 reserves 27, and 80 reserves 41. This matches the "up to 50" and "half of `gaps_out` plus 1" in the new docs.
- `bar-test.sh` (132 checks) and `bar-text-color-test.sh` pass on the head. The head's `bar-test.sh` fails on the earlier head's code, where `windowMargins` and `exclusiveZone` do not exist yet. Each of the five earlier breakages, as reproduced here, now fails `bar-test.sh`.

### Test coverage of the popout fix

**Optional test improvement:** The new popout and toast handling is checked only by matching source text (`bar-test.sh`, the `KeyboardPanel`/`Service.qml` regexes). In diagnostic copies of the head, six edits that undo parts of it still passed `bar-test.sh`:
- forcing `KeyboardPanel`'s `barMargins` to zeros (a full revert of the popout fix)
- restoring the old top-card `y`
- dropping the margin from `barY`
- dropping `barEdgeMargin` from `_barStripSize`
- setting the toast `liveBarMargin` to 0
- removing the `api.barMargins` binding

A behaviour-preserving rewrite of `barX` failed it. Two close variants of the earlier breakages also still pass: the radius not applied through the `barRadius` binding, and `bar.floating` ignored in the `floating` binding. Moving the bar-origin, card-placement and toast-clearance arithmetic into small `BarModel`-style functions with value tests, as the PR now does for `windowMargins` and `exclusiveZone`, would cover the six edits above. The two binding variants need their own check of how `floating` and `barRadius` are fed.

### Plugin bar facade omits `barMargins`

`shell/services/PluginBarStateApi.qml`, the `shell.bar` view given to non-first-party plugins that position their own windows, exposes `barHidden`, `barSize`, `fontFamily` and `position` but no `barMargins`. Bar widgets get the margins through `PluginBarApi`; these plugins do not.

**Impact:** A plugin that places a window the way the built-in toasts now do reads a 0 margin and sits against or over a floating bar, as the built-in toasts did before this revision. Whether such plugins exist today was not checked.

**Suggested change:** Add `barMargins` to that facade and bind it in `shell.qml` next to the other four.

### Documentation

- `shell/plugins/bar/README.md:51` ("which do not move") and `default/agents/skills/omarchy/plugins.md:40` ("Windows do not move when floating is toggled") still state window stability without the large-`gaps_out` condition now given in `docs/omarchy-shell.md`.
- In that condition, "half of `gaps_out` stays below the bar's thickness" is one value off at `gaps_out = 51`: half is 25.5, but the margin rounds to 26, so windows move by 1 px. The "up to 50" figure is right.
- **Optional:** listing `bar.barMargins` in the widget property lists (`README.md` "Bar properties available to widgets", `docs/omarchy-shell.md`) would let widget authors find the new property.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up source review of head `ced6275` against the earlier reviewed head `3d04c27` and merge-base `28ceaae`, including the Quickshell 0.3.1 and Hyprland 0.56.2 source that the placement depends on. The repository's bar tests, the diagnostic mutations and an evaluation of the popout and toast placement expressions extracted from the head and base code ran in an isolated command-line sandbox under Node. No compositor or shell was launched. Rendered placement and click forwarding were not observed on screen, and the author's nested-Hyprland check was not reproduced. The model assumes no other exclusive layer surface offsets the bar, as the base code does.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
